Plan how your team will run the website

When scoping website development services, choose the platform based on how content changes, how customers buy and which systems the site needs to connect to.

Editable business sites

Use website development services to plan page templates and content types around your team’s needs. WordPress or another content management system can let authorised staff update copy, images and articles without editing code.

Online stores

E-commerce website development can use Shopify or WooCommerce, depending on your catalogue, checkout and back-office tools. Agree pricing, inventory, shipping and returns so the store and the team managing orders work from the same rules.

Custom and connected sites

Build custom features where the project needs account areas, booking rules or data from another system. For a wallet-connected site, scope the supported network and user journey separately. Show which actions require a signature and how users can recover from an interrupted transaction.

Explore ongoing store operations

Set up integrations, search and measurement

Agree which actions matter to your business and how to verify that enquiries, bookings and orders reach the right system.

Enquiries, bookings and payments

Connect each form or purchase path to the approved destination. During e-commerce website development, test abandoned checkout, failed payments and notifications so customers and staff can tell whether the order went through.

Search at launch

Website development services can include page titles, internal links, crawl checks and a sitemap. During website redesign and migration, carry over useful content and map changed URLs. Set up Search Console if it is part of the release.

Analytics around business actions

When measurement is in scope, configure events for agreed actions such as a completed booking or order. Test which events fire, and confirm the privacy and cookie settings before enabling visitor tracking.

Explore SEO and WordPress support

Launch the site and make it easy to maintain

Use a staging site to review real content and key journeys. For website redesign and migration, give each launch action and follow-up check an owner.

Review before switching

Share the preview with the people who approve the content, technical setup and redirects. For website redesign and migration, coordinate the domain or hosting switch and agree when the old site can be retired.

Handover and editorial training

Walk through the page editor, access roles, where enquiries arrive and how to request a change. Document the repository, hosting and deployment steps so someone else can pick up the work.

Website maintenance and support

Agree how to handle updates, backups, fixes and new work. Identify who checks the site after updates and how your team will report problems such as forms that stop routing or checkout errors.

When this support helps

A new site for a service business

Use website development services to organise services by customer need and give each page a clear next step. Test where enquiries go and who takes ownership when one arrives.

Replace a site without losing key pages

Start website redesign and migration with an inventory of live URLs, popular pages and legacy features. Keep a mapping for the pages that move and verify the important redirects after switching.

Launch a shop with a manageable catalogue

For e-commerce website development, start with a representative range of products. Check variants, stock status, payment, confirmation emails and what the team sees in the order queue.

How the work gets done

  1. 01

    Plan the pages and features

    Scope website development services around your audience, what visitors need to do and the content or product records you already have. Set approval points for design, functionality and anything that needs to move.

  2. 02

    Design, build and review

    Review layouts, then check the working site in staging. For website redesign and migration, ask the people who publish pages, receive leads or manage orders to test how their work will continue.

  3. 03

    Launch and train the team

    Complete the agreed release checks and confirm permissions, hosting and support ownership. Plan further work under the agreed website maintenance and support scope.

Release checks for website development services

  • Test navigation, forms and checkout on representative phone and desktop sizes.
  • Review keyboard navigation, form labels and clear error messages.
  • Check images, scripts and font loading on the pages visitors use most.
  • Verify live redirects, canonical URLs, the sitemap and search settings where in scope.
  • Confirm who owns hosting, domain access, deployments, backups and future updates.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you build a new site and take over an existing one?

Yes. For a new site, we scope the pages and features first. For website redesign and migration, we review the live content, URLs, forms and hosting before planning the changes.

Can our team edit the site after launch?

Yes, if editing is part of the project. We set up content fields and publishing permissions so authorised staff can make routine updates. The handover shows which changes need development.

Can you build an online store with our existing tools?

E-commerce website development can connect your store with agreed payment, stock, order and shipping tools. We check compatibility and test a purchase and the order handoff before launch.

Do you include SEO and analytics?

Website development services can include technical search setup, metadata, redirects and agreed analytics events. We scope the work around the project and confirm when tracking can be enabled.

What affects development cost and timing?

The cost of website development services depends on templates, supplied content, catalogue size, integrations and review time. A staged release can help you prioritise the pages and features you need first.

Can you keep the site updated after release?

Website maintenance and support can cover the agreed updates, backups, bug fixes and compatibility checks. We confirm responsibilities and what counts as a separate feature before work begins.
